title: Author of Faith, Eternal Word
description: Author of Faith, Eternal Word in Tonic Solfa to UXBRIDGE, doh is E: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 6 verses and a piano.
about: John Wesley printed these words in A Collection of Hymns for the Use of the People Called Methodists (1780), hymn 95. They first appeared in a book he and his brother Charles published together, and the Collection's own index cannot say which of the two wrote them.
The book printed the words without tunes. They are in Long Metre (8.8.8.8), and this page sets them to UXBRIDGE; any other Long Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Au-thor of faith, e-ter-nal Word, Whose Spir-it breathes the ac-tive flame: Faith, like its Fin-ish-er and Lord, To day as yes-ter-day the same;

lines: Author of faith, eternal Word,
Whose Spirit breathes the active flame:
Faith, like its Finisher and Lord,
To-day as yesterday the same;
To thee our humble hearts aspire,
And ask the gift unspeakable;
Increase in us the kindled fire,
In us the work of faith fulfil.
By faith we know thee strong to save;
(Save us, a present Saviour thou!)
Whate'er we hope, by faith we have,
Future and past subsisting now.
To him that in thy name believes
Eternal life with thee is given;
Into himself he all receives,
Pardon, and holiness, and heaven.
The things unknown to feeble sense,
Unseen by reason's glimmering ray,
With strong, commanding evidence,
Their heavenly origin display.
Faith lends its realizing light,
The clouds disperse, the shadows fly;
The Invisible appears in sight,
And God is seen by mortal eye.

source: John Wesley, A Collection of Hymns for the Use of the People Called Methodists (1780)
licence: Public domain: Charles Wesley died in 1788; John Wesley died in 1791.
credits: Words by Charles Wesley (1707–1788) or John Wesley (1703–1791), public domain, as printed in John Wesley's Collection of Hymns (1780); set to UXBRIDGE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
